Know the Persian Wars (490–479 BCE): a conflict between Greece and Persia
Know the Athenian Empire (479–431/404 BCE): emerged from the Delian League; the Golden Age of Athens; rise of the Athenian navy
Know the Peloponnesian War (431–404 BCE): a conflict between Athens and Sparta
Know the Rise of Macedon: Philip II attacked Greek city-states; Alexander extended Greek rule to its furthest extent
Know the Hellenistic Age: the period following the death of Alexander the Great (after 323 BCE)
Know Darius I (the Great): a Persian leader who died in 485 BCE; associated with the Persian Wars
Know Xerxes: son of Darius I; Persian leader during the Persian Wars
Know Leonidas: a Spartan king who commanded the 300 Spartans at Thermopylae
Know Pericles: Athenian statesman and general who died in 429 BCE; promoted Athens as a cultural center and fostered Athenian democracy
Know Philip II of Macedon: a warlord who attacked Greek city-states; father of Alexander the Great
Know Alexander the Great: son of Philip of Macedon, died in 323 BCE; extended Greek rule to its furthest extent
Know the Battle of Marathon (490 BCE): Greeks defeated the Persians on the plain of Marathon; Athenians asked Spartans for help but they declined
Know the Battle of Thermopylae (480 BCE): 300 Spartans under Leonidas prevented the Persians from invading at a narrow pass
Know the Battle of Salamis (480 BCE): the Greek navy defeated the Persian navy
Know the Peace of Nicias (421 BCE): a treaty meant to end the Peloponnesian War but was subsequently undermined
Know the Battle of Aegospotami (405 BCE): Spartan navy destroyed the Athenian navy, ending the Peloponnesian War
Know the Battle of Chaeronea (338 BCE): Philip II defeated Athens and Thebes, resulting in the League of Corinth
Know the Battle of Issus (333 BCE): Alexander led the Hellenic League against the Achaemenid Empire under Darius III
Know the Battle of Gaugamela (331 BCE): Alexander and the Hellenic League decisively defeated Darius III

Know Plato: philosopher who wrote about Socrates' philosophical dialogues; famous works include The Republic (on the ideal state) and the Apology (Socrates' defense against corrupting the youth of Athens)
Know Aeschylus: called 'The Father of Tragedy'; produced the Oresteia trilogy about Agamemnon's son
Know Sophocles: never judged lower than 2nd place in dramatic competitions; produced Oedipus the King and Oedipus at Colonus about the tragic king of Thebes
Know Euripides: produced Medea (about the witch married to the Argonaut Jason) and Hippolytus (on the tragic death of Theseus' son)
Know Herodotus: called 'The Father of History'; author of The Histories on the origins of the Persian Wars
Know Thucydides: author of the History of the Peloponnesian War
Know Zeus: king of the gods; spheres include lightning and thunder; symbols are the eagle and lightning bolt
Know Hera: queen of the gods; sphere is marriage; symbol is the peacock
Know Poseidon: god of oceans, water, and earthquakes; symbols are the trident and horse
Know Hades: ruler of the Underworld; symbol is the bident
Know Demeter: goddess of agriculture; symbols are the stalk of wheat and cornucopia
Know Hestia: goddess of the hearth (home fire); symbols are the hearth and small fire
Know Ares: god of war; symbols are the spear and vulture
Know Athena: goddess of wisdom, war, and domestic crafts/tasks; symbols are the owl, helmet, olive branch/tree, and aegis
Know Hephaestus: god of blacksmithing and metalworking; symbols are the hammer and anvil
Know Apollo: god of the sun, prophecy, music, and medicine; symbols are the sun, bow and arrows, and lyre
Know Artemis: goddess of the moon, hunting, and animals; symbols are the moon, bow and arrows, deer, and hunting dog
Know Hermes: god of messengers, thieves, and inventors; symbols are the caduceus (winged staff with serpents) and winged sandals
Know Dionysus: god of wine, revelry, and insanity; symbols are grapes, grape vines, ivy, leopards, and the thyrsus (pinecone-topped staff)
Know Aphrodite: goddess of love and beauty; symbols are doves and erotes (winged babies)
